import pandas as pd

# Paths to source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_65/training_7.csv",
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# All source tables have the same schema and match the target schema exactly,
# so we can union (concatenate) them directly.
df_union = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure correct dtypes according to target schema:
# Target schema:
# ['movie_display_name': string,
#  'movie_production_year': integer,
#  'movie_genre_display_name': string,
#  'movie_financial_summary_production_budget': integer,
#  'movie_financial_summary_international_box_office': integer,
#  'movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold': float,
#  'movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units': float,
#  'movie_acting_role_display_name': string,
#  'movie_theatrical_release_release_date': string,
#  'movie_creative_type_display_name': string,
#  'movie_production_method_display_name': string,
#  'movie_source_display_name': string,
#  'movie_running_time': float,
#  'movie_technical_role_display_name': string,
#  'movie_production_company_display_name': string,
#  'movie_sequel': integer]

# Convert columns to appropriate types:
# For integer columns, convert with pd.to_numeric and downcast if possible.
# For float columns, convert with pd.to_numeric.
# For string columns, convert with astype(str), but keep NaNs as is.

# Define columns by type
int_cols = [
    "movie_production_year",
    "movie_financial_summary_production_budget",
    "movie_financial_summary_international_box_office",
    "movie_sequel",
]
float_cols = [
    "movie_annual_summary_tickets_sold",
    "movie_video_summary_domestic_dvd_units",
    "movie_running_time",
]
string_cols = [
    "movie_display_name",
    "movie_genre_display_name",
    "movie_acting_role_display_name",
    "movie_theatrical_release_release_date",
    "movie_creative_type_display_name",
    "movie_production_method_display_name",
    "movie_source_display_name",
    "movie_technical_role_display_name",
    "movie_production_company_display_name",
]

# Convert integer columns: some may have floats or NaNs, so convert carefully
for col in int_cols:
    # Convert to numeric, coerce errors, then convert to Int64 (nullable integer)
    df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Convert float columns
for col in float_cols:
    df_union[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_union[col], errors='coerce')

# Convert string columns: convert to string but keep NaNs as is
for col in string_cols:
    # If column is not object, convert to string, else keep as is
    # But NaNs should remain NaN, so use .where + astype(str)
    df_union[col] = df_union[col].where(df_union[col].notna(), None)
    df_union[col] = df_union[col].astype("string")

# After type conversion, fill missing movie_running_time with NaN float (already float)
# No further imputation needed as per instructions.

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_65/target_multisource.csv"
df_union.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
